title: Udayan Movement Launched in Mumbai to Form 1,000 Young Institution Builders by 2036
summary: Mentors from academia, governance, industry and the social sector met the first Udayan School of Social Leadership cohort in Mumbai to launch a ten-year youth leadership movement.
body_html:
Mumbai, 27 October 2026: A founding circle of mentors gathered in Mumbai on Saturday, 10 October, to launch the Udayan Movement, a ten-year national effort to form young leaders who will build enterprises and institutions for the India of 2047. The circle sat with students of the first cohort of the Udayan School of Social Leadership (USSL), Pune.

The founding circle included vice chancellors of universities, leadership mentors to CxOs, CSR and social impact strategists, business founders, serial entrepreneurs, lawyers and administrators. The organisers described the gathering as drawing on all four stages of life in Bharat's ashram tradition, with experienced mentors sitting alongside young learners, in line with the movement's belief that nation-building begins with human development.

The movement aims to form 1,000 young institution builders over the next ten years, along with 5,000 more founders mentored in their communities. The organisers point out that by 2046 about 14.58 crore of today's children and young people will be seeking work, and that alongside skilling, the country needs young people who can create work for others.

"As USSL's first patron, I have seen what these students can do. What moved me in Mumbai was that the support in the room was not only capital. It was time, judgment and belonging, from people at every stage of life, given to young people who have not yet earned a thing from us. That is how a society invests in its future," said Jayesh Shah, Social Equity Entrepreneur and First Patron of USSL.

USSL in Pune is a five-year, full-time leadership programme for students after Grade 10. It is part of the Wonder School Learning Collective and builds on 15 years of Potters Earth Foundation's work with about 2 lakh students and 50,000 teachers. Its approach is rooted in the Arthashastra, Nyaya Darshan and the Gurukul tradition.

Over several months, the first cohort studied the Viksit Bharat 2047 documents, attended lectures on law and governance and masterclasses by industry veterans, and carried out field research in communities. Their enterprise ideas include AnnaGati (moving safe surplus food to nutritionally insecure city communities), BeejSwaraj (helping farmers keep more of the value they create), DishaSetu (career guidance and skills for young people), FishLoops (recovering value from fish waste in Pune's markets) and Voice of Cashew (turning wasted cashew apples and shells into income for women). Each idea is tested on whether it is ethical, financially viable and legal and fair to every stakeholder.

"In CSR, we usually ask what a programme will deliver in a year. The Udayan Movement asks what a generation will build in ten years," said Saurabh Sharma, CSR and Social Impact Strategist. The founding circle will continue to work with the students to take each idea from research towards a working social enterprise.
